observations: Photo 0 shows a Caterpillar-style industrial engine block with exposed top/side components, hoses, and wiring harnesses; no obvious model plate is readable.
Photo 1 shows the top/valve cover area of the same engine with a large cast cover and multiple ports; again, no clearly readable engine ID/model markings.
Both photos appear to show an engine assembly being sold as parts (not a complete installed running unit), but condition (leaks, cracks, missing parts) is not fully verifiable from these angles.

claims.evidence: The photos show an engine assembly, but the C9 model identification is not readable (no clear ID plate/label visible). Also, 'complete' cannot be confirmed from only two angles.

risks.risk: Engine model may not be C9 (could be another Caterpillar engine family with similar layout).
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the engine serial/model plate (or stamped engine number) with readable text.
risks.if_unproven: Price as generic Caterpillar engine parts (worst-case: not confirmed C9), typically valued lower than confirmed C9 parts.

risks.risk: Not actually complete: missing key components (turbo, injectors, sensors, ECM, alternator, starter, fuel system parts).
risks.proof: A full parts inventory photo list: lay out all major components and take a video walk-through showing everything included.
risks.if_unproven: Price as incomplete engine parts (worst-case: missing major electronics/fuel components), not as a complete engine.

risks.risk: Internal damage (cracked block/head, scored cylinders, bent rods) not visible externally.
risks.proof: Photos of cylinder bores and crankshaft area (or compression test / teardown report).
risks.if_unproven: Price as parts only with unknown internal condition (worst-case: not usable for rebuild).

risks.risk: Unknown condition of wiring harness/sensors/ECM (often fails even if engine casting looks intact).
risks.proof: Close-ups of ECM/ECU label and photos of all sensors/connectors; include a test/bench check if available.
risks.if_unproven: Price as non-tested electrical components (worst-case: not working).

risks.risk: Compatibility risk: even if C9, some parts may be from different configurations/years (aftertreatment, fuel system variants).
risks.proof: Provide engine serial number and parts list/part numbers for key components.
risks.if_unproven: Price with reduced value due to variant uncertainty (worst-case: limited interchangeability).

proof_requests: Close-up, readable photo of the engine ID/model plate or stamped engine number (for C9 confirmation).
A clear photo/video showing all included parts laid out (to confirm 'complete').
Photos of cylinder head/valve cover underside and cylinder bores (or any teardown evidence).
Close-ups of ECM/ECU and major sensors/injectors with readable part numbers.
Any proof of prior running condition (video of start/run or service history), if they have it.
response.reason: The photos show a Caterpillar-style engine assembly, but the C9 model and 'complete' status are not readable/confirmable from the provided images. Without the engine ID/serial and a parts inventory, a safe worst-case price cannot be determined.
